transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-09 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 55m
Attendees: Maria Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM), Ethan Morales (Cobalt Head of ML), Sara Iqbal (Cobalt Platform Eng), Jordan Lee (Cobalt Product), Priya Singh (Cobalt Security)
---
[00:00] Maria Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Maria from Redwood, with Daniel and Priya on our side. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Ethan Morales: Good, thanks. Busy prep for the holiday spike, that's why this is important.
[00:18] Maria Chen: Totally. High level agenda: adoption/usage trends, capacity forecast for the next 6 months, reliability & security items, then next steps. We'll leave time for Q&A.
[00:30] Jordan Lee: Sounds good.
[01:05] Priya Rao: I'll jump in on adoption signals as we go — we pulled the last 90 days of token usage and MAU across their storefronts.
[01:20] Daniel Park: I'll cover the capacity options and performance tradeoffs — hosted, dedicated, private.
[01:33] Sara Iqbal: Quick note from infra — our network team needs specifics on outbound ports and peering before the end of next week.
[01:40] Maria Chen: Noted. We'll put that in the action items.
---
[02:10] Priya Rao: Adoption: Cobalt's monthly active endpoints rose 42% quarter-over-quarter, a lot of the growth driven by the new recommendations flow and chatbot on checkout. Token volume spiked 3x during promo events. We're seeing heavier long-context calls for order summarization which affects sequence length distribution.
[02:45] Ethan Morales: Right, the summarization prompts run up to 2k tokens occasionally. That increased tail latency.
[02:57] Daniel Park: That matters for kernel selection and batching. For long sequences, some of our LLM kernels trade throughput for memory; dedicated GPU pools can give you predictable p99 latency.
[03:15] Jordan Lee: Can you quantify "predictable"? We care about 95th and 99th latency for checkout flows.
[03:28] Daniel Park: Based on similar customers, Dedicated with pinned replicas we see p95 ~120-220ms for short prompts, p99 for long-2k style calls can be 500-800ms depending on batch window. Hosted can be variable — sometimes lower median, but p99 spikes under heavy load.
[03:52] Priya Singh: From security perspective we need SLA for data isolation — we can't have cross-tenant KV cache leakage.
[04:05] Maria Chen: Absolutely — Dedicated and Private options give isolation. For hosted we offer strong multi-tenancy controls and encryption at rest, but the customer requirement sounds like Dedicated or Private.
---
[05:00] Sara Iqbal: Our network constraints: strict egress rules, we have an internal proxy. Can Redwood support establishing a VPC peering or private link?
[05:15] Daniel Park: Yes, we support VPC peering and private endpoints. We'll share the network checklist. There may be additional firewall rules for metrics and tracing endpoints.
[05:27] Ethan Morales: Great. Also curious about cost: currently we run a managed model on BigCloudAI, and invoices are unpredictable during spikes. How do you model holiday capacity vs cost?
[05:44] Maria Chen: We usually run two analyses: baseline usage + spike percentile and a stress test. For holiday, you can either overcommit reserved capacity (lower unit cost) or rely on burst-backing into hosted capacity. The right mix depends on your tolerance for p99 spikes and unit economics.
[06:05] Jordan Lee: Cost numbers would help — e.g., delta per 1M tokens between hosted and reserved.
[06:12] Maria Chen: We'll send your tailored Q3 pricing sheet with modeled examples.
---
[07:00] Daniel Park: Technical deep dive: batching window tuning — if you allow a 10–15ms batching window you can reduce per-token cost but add to latency. For checkout we recommend 0–5ms to keep tail latency tight. For background tasks like catalog summarization you can use larger windows.
[07:30] Ethan Morales: Hmm, checkout can't have extra latency. We're aiming p95 < 200ms. Is that realistic with reserved GPUs?
[07:42] Daniel Park: Yes, with dedicated pools and kernel optimizations, and aggressive caching for common prefixes, p95 < 200ms is achievable. We also suggested prefix/KV caching for the summarization flow to reduce repeat decoding.
---
[08:15] Priya Singh: Compliance: we require evidence of SOC2, SSO integration points (SAML/OIDC), RBAC, and HSM-backed KMS for keys. Also an audit trail for inference calls.
[08:32] Maria Chen: Redwood has SOC2 reports and SAML SSO support; we integrate with KMS providers and offer audit logs for inference calls and key usage. We'll share the security pack and an anonymized audit log schema for review.
[08:50] Priya Singh: Data residency? Some EU customers demand logs stay in-region.
[08:57] Maria Chen: We support region pinning for hosted, and Private deployments can be fully in-region or on-prem. We'll document the retention controls.
---
[09:40] Jordan Lee: On pilot scope — we'd like a 4-week pilot targeting our recommendations API and checkout summarizer. What success criteria should we use?
[09:55] Daniel Park: Suggested success criteria: 1) p95 latency under target (200ms for checkout), 2) per-token cost within X% of modeled committed rate, 3) no security exceptions in ingress/egress tests, 4) pass load test at 2x expected peak.
[10:20] Ethan Morales: Also add error rate and model quality thresholds — we can't degrade conversion by more than 1.5%.
[10:28] Maria Chen: Good call. We'll bake that into the pilot metrics.
---
[11:05] Priya Rao: Adoption note: the chatbot has a 15% conversion uplift in A/B tests but uses more tokens. So there's a direct revenue vs cost tradeoff. We recommended per-route routing so high-value flows use reserved low-latency endpoints while exploratory/low-value flows stay hosted.
[11:30] Jordan Lee: Is that routing policy easy to manage? We have multiple teams that need separate budgets.
[11:36] Maria Chen: The Console supports per-route budgets and model pins; you can set fallback policies and routing rules. We'll share a sample routing config.
---
[12:20] Sara Iqbal: For private deploy, what's the estimated lead time?
[12:28] Daniel Park: For a standard VPC/private plane, about 4–6 weeks including security review and network setup. On-prem can be longer depending on hardware procurement.
[12:40] Priya Singh: And what about software updates/patching cadence? We need upgrade windows documented.
[12:48] Maria Chen: We'll include our maintenance windows and optional controlled upgrade schedule for Private deployments.
---
[13:30] Ethan Morales: One question — we evaluated Hyperserve; they offered cheaper token rates but no KV cache and poorer observability. How does Redwood's observability help us avoid cost creep?
[13:46] Daniel Park: Observability gives you token-level breakdowns, route-level spend, and tracing hooks to find hot prompts. That helps identify optimization targets; combined with Optimize recommendations (quantization/batching) it's usually more impactful than chasing raw unit price.
[14:05] Priya Rao: Also our regressions alerts can detect model quality drift tied to prompt sets — so you avoid rollouts that suddenly increase token usage or lower conversion.
---
[14:40] Jordan Lee: Any gotchas we should watch for during pilot?
[14:45] Daniel Park: Watch sequence-length distribution; a small fraction of super-long calls can blow out memory unless you configure limits or separate long-tail flows to different pool. Also pre-warm KV caches before peak.
[15:00] Priya Singh: We'll need a security checklist and an initial penetration test plan.
[15:05] Maria Chen: We'll include a recommended pentest scope in the security pack.
---
[16:00] Wrap-up / Recap:
Maria Chen: Recap — action items: we'll send pricing and capacity forecast, Daniel will send network & private deployment checklist, Cobalt will send 7-day traces and prompt sets, and we'll aim to start a 4-week pilot end of September. Pilot success criteria include latency, cost delta, quality thresholds, and load tests.
[16:30] Ethan Morales: That aligns. Looking forward to the pricing scenarios.
[16:35] Jordan Lee: Please include a breakdown by route so we can see checkout vs recommendations separately.
[16:40] Priya Rao: Noted, we'll split the model and routing costs by route.
[17:00] Maria Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites and docs.
[17:10] Priya Singh: Thanks.
